cands.name: Gregg Mele

top: CREDIT PORTFOLIO MANAGER · Glen Rock, NJ
money.note: Individuals gave $44,275; PAC money $3,500; candidate's own money $53,746. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for New Jersey's 12th Congressional District in 2026. Ballotpedia lists his profession as educator, with a law degree from New York Law School and several graduate degrees. His campaign says he worked in law, business, finance, technology and teaching. He has run for office several times and has not held office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Gregg Mele was born or raised, or when he moved to New Jersey. His career in law, business, finance and teaching is described only by his campaign and could not be checked against an independent source. He has held no elected office, so there is no voting record. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, land protection, homestead property taxes, abortion or restrictions on foreign or investor buyers of land. We found no news reporting on controversies and no listed endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any of his recent races. The pages we had gave no reason he was disqualified from the 2022 primary.

qual.background: Ballotpedia lists him as an educator with a bachelor's from Montclair State and a law degree from New York Law School. It also lists graduate study at Stevens, NYU Law and Baruch. His campaign site says he built a career in law, business, finance, technology and the classroom. He has never held elected office and has run for Congress and governor several times.
qual.why: He has no governing or legislative experience. His legal, business and teaching background comes mostly from his own campaign description, and the details of those jobs could not be verified. That puts him in the lower-middle range.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2024 campaign website (for a different race) said a simple NICS check should be enough for a gun permit, with no local police process. It also promised to push concealed carry and reciprocity and to block state and local limits on gun rights.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His 2024 and 2021 campaign websites called for school choice, including home schooling, with tax funding following the student. The 2024 site also said underperforming public schools should lose funding.

workers-first.evidence: His 2026 campaign platform says he would restore operational control at the border and enforce existing immigration law, while supporting legal immigration. His 2024 site said sanctuary policies should lead to removal from office.

back-police-order.evidence: His 2026 campaign platform says he would support police, firefighters and emergency personnel and put neighborhood safety first.

cands.bio: Plastic surgeon with a practice in Princeton and a small business owner. Retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel who served as a combat surgeon in Iraq. Has volunteered as a physician in disaster and war zones, including Gaza in 2024. Has not held elected office before.

controversies.text: In 1995 Hamawy testified under oath for the defense at Omar Abdel-Rahman's terrorism trial. He said he saw the cleric at mosques and in his home, shared a room with him on a 1991 trip and translated for him in 1993. Of jihad he said, "Of course. That's what he always talked about." In 2026 the New Jersey Monitor reported that he "maintains he had no relationship." A claim that he lied under oath is unproven: we found no court or official finding. His campaign called the coverage "bad-faith, guilt-by-association attacks."

endorsements.text: U.S. Sens. Tammy Duckworth and Bernie Sanders, Justice Democrats PAC, Our Revolution, CAIR Action, Emgage Action and A New Policy PAC, per Ballotpedia.
Outgoing Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, per his campaign site.
Reps. Ro Khanna and Ilhan Omar, former Rep. Jamaal Bowman and former Assemblymember Sadaf Jaffer, per Wikipedia.

cands.gaps: Hamawy has never held elected office, so there is no voting record or official action to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or land use, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, police pay and pensions, or gun laws. The campaign site's issue page was cut off partway through the civil rights section, so anything after that was not read. His exact birth year and the year his family moved to New Jersey are not given beyond 'as a baby.'

qual.background: Army Medical Corps surgeon for eight years (rose to lieutenant colonel, served in Iraq), then plastic surgeon who built his own Princeton practice; holds an MBA from Rutgers–Camden. No prior elected or legislative office.
qual.why: He has real-world management experience as a practice owner and officer, but no legislative, legal, budget or governing experience, and his main occupation is medicine, which is not directly related to lawmaking.

clean-money.evidence: Says he has committed to refusing corporate PAC money on his campaign and describes the race as people-powered with no corporate PAC money.

pro-life.evidence: Says he supports codifying the right to abortion in federal law and that politicians should stay out of decisions between doctors and patients.

workers-first.evidence: Campaigns on abolishing ICE, dismantling DHS and a path to citizenship for undocumented people, and says he will protect DACA recipients and mixed-status families from deportation.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he supports increasing teacher pay, including a federal salary floor for teachers. His stated education focus is on public schools, and the pages say nothing about vouchers or charters.
